# Filemark — Chrome Web Store publishing runbook

Step-by-step for the two things you'll ever do:

1. **First publish** — getting the extension onto the Web Store once
2. **Update releases** — every version bump after that

All commands assume you're in the repo root:
`/Volumes/D/www/projects/khanakia/chrome-extensions/filemark`.

---

## Part 1 — First-time publish (do this once)

The one-time setup has four phases: dev-account → extension draft →
API credentials → first submission.

### 1.1 Register a Chrome Web Store developer account

1. Go to <https://chrome.google.com/webstore/devconsole>.
2. Sign in with the Google account that should own the listing
   (`amank@solverhood.com` or a team Google Workspace account).
3. Pay the one-time **$5 USD** developer registration fee.
4. Accept the Developer Agreement.

> You cannot publish anything until this fee clears. It takes a few
> minutes.

### 1.2 Create the listing (draft with placeholder zip)

The Web Store needs at least one uploaded zip before it will issue an
extension ID. So do a dummy upload first:

1. Build and zip locally:
   ```bash
   task build
   task zip
   task zip:verify
   ```
   This produces `filemark.zip` at repo root.

2. In the dev-console, click **New Item** → drop `filemark.zip` in the
   upload box.

3. The dashboard now shows a 32-character extension ID in the URL, e.g.
   `https://chrome.google.com/webstore/devconsole/.../abcdefghijklmnopabcdefghijklmnop/`.
   **Copy that ID** — that's your `CWS_EXTENSION_ID`.

4. Fill in the listing metadata:
   - **Store listing** — description, screenshots (min. 1, max. 5,
     1280×800 or 640×400), promo tiles.
   - **Privacy practices** — single-purpose statement, permission
     justifications for `storage`, `activeTab`, `file:///*`.
   - **Distribution** — category: "Developer Tools", regions: all,
     visibility: public.

> Save as draft. Don't submit yet.

### 1.3 Create Google Cloud OAuth credentials

Needed to automate uploads from the Taskfile.

1. Open <https://console.cloud.google.com/>.
2. Top bar → **New Project** → name it `filemark-cws` (or reuse an
   existing one).
3. Sidebar → **APIs & Services** → **Library** → search for
   **"Chrome Web Store API"** → click → **Enable**.
4. Sidebar → **APIs & Services** → **OAuth consent screen**:
   - User type: **External**
   - App name: `Filemark Publisher`
   - Support email: your email
   - Scopes: skip (default is fine)
   - Test users: add the Google account that owns the Web Store listing
   - Save
5. Sidebar → **APIs & Services** → **Credentials** → **+ Create
   Credentials** → **OAuth client ID**:
   - Application type: **Desktop app**
   - Name: `filemark-cli`
   - Create → copy the **Client ID** and **Client secret** shown in the
     dialog. These are `CWS_CLIENT_ID` and `CWS_CLIENT_SECRET`.

### 1.4 Generate a refresh token

The refresh token lets the CLI upload without opening a browser each
time. One-time dance:

1. Visit this URL in your browser (replace `<CLIENT_ID>`):
   ```
   https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth?response_type=code&scope=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/chromewebstore&client_id=<CLIENT_ID>&redirect_uri=urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob
   ```
2. Sign in with the Web Store account. Approve the scopes. Google shows
   an **authorization code** on-screen — copy it.

3. Exchange the code for a refresh token:
   ```bash
   curl "https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/token" \
     -d "client_id=<CLIENT_ID>" \
     -d "client_secret=<CLIENT_SECRET>" \
     -d "code=<AUTH_CODE>" \
     -d "grant_type=authorization_code" \
     -d "redirect_uri=urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob"
   ```
4. The JSON response contains a `"refresh_token": "1//0gR..."` — copy
   it. That's `CWS_REFRESH_TOKEN`.

> Refresh tokens don't expire unless you revoke access. Store this
> somewhere safe (1Password, etc.).

### 1.5 Populate `.env`

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

Fill in the four values you just collected:

```
CWS_EXTENSION_ID=abcdefghijklmnopabcdefghijklmnop
CWS_CLIENT_ID=1234567890-xxx.apps.googleusercontent.com
CWS_CLIENT_SECRET=GOCSPX-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
CWS_REFRESH_TOKEN=1//0gRxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

`.env` is gitignored — it will never be committed.

### 1.6 Submit for review

1. Finalize the listing in the dev-console (screenshots, descriptions,
   privacy practices — all green checkmarks).
2. From the terminal:
   ```bash
   task cws:publish
   ```
   This re-zips the current build and submits for public review.

3. Check the dashboard: **Status** will flip to **Pending review**.
   Google typically responds within 1–3 business days.

Once approved, the extension is live at
`https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/<CWS_EXTENSION_ID>`.

---

## Part 2 — Shipping an update (every subsequent release)

After the first publish, every new version is a three-command ritual.

### 2.1 Decide the version bump

Follow semver:

| Change type | Bump |
|---|---|
| Bug fix, tiny tweak | patch (0.1.0 → 0.1.1) |
| New feature, new format, new shortcut | minor (0.1.0 → 0.2.0) |
| Breaking change (storage schema, removed feature) | major (0.1.0 → 1.0.0) |

Check current version:
```bash
task version
```

### 2.2 Merge your changes

Make sure:
- All work is committed to `main`
- `task typecheck` passes
- `task build` passes
- You've manually tested the extension in an unpacked install
  (`chrome://extensions` → "Load unpacked" → `apps/chrome-ext/dist`)

### 2.3 Run the release pipeline

One command does everything:

```bash
task release -- 0.2.0
```

This:
1. Bumps the version in `manifest.json`, `package.json`, and every
   workspace `package.json`
2. Cleans old build artifacts
3. Rebuilds all packages + the extension
4. Packages into `filemark.zip`
5. Verifies the zip has the required entries
6. Uploads to the Web Store
7. Submits for public review

### 2.4 Commit the version bump

The `version:bump` step edits files — commit those:

```bash
git add manifest.json apps/chrome-ext/public/manifest.json \
        package.json apps/chrome-ext/package.json packages/*/package.json
git commit -m "Release v0.2.0"
git tag v0.2.0
git push origin main --tags
```

### 2.5 Monitor review

```bash
task dashboard
```

Watch for the status change. If Google rejects, the email/console
explains why — fix it, bump the patch version, and repeat `task
release -- 0.2.1`.

---

## Troubleshooting

### Upload fails with `400 INVALID_DEVELOPER` or `FORBIDDEN`

Your refresh token is tied to a different Google account than the one
that owns the listing. Regenerate the token from step 1.4 while signed
in to the correct account.

### Upload fails with `ITEM_NOT_FOUND`

`CWS_EXTENSION_ID` is wrong. Copy it fresh from the dashboard URL.

### Review rejected — "uses remote code"

MV3 forbids fetching + eval'ing remote JS. We already avoid this
(Shiki uses static JSON, no dynamic `import()` from URLs). If rejected,
check recent changes for new `<script src="https://...">` tags,
`fetch(...).then(eval)`, etc.

### Review rejected — "unnecessary permissions"

Audit `manifest.json` → `permissions`. Only `storage`, `activeTab`,
`sidePanel` should be there. `host_permissions` should only list
`file:///*`. Justify each in the listing's **Privacy practices** page.

### Review rejected — "single purpose"

The Web Store requires every extension to have one clearly-stated
purpose. Our purpose: *"View local markdown, MDX, JSON, and database
schema files inside Chrome."* Keep the listing text aligned with that.

### Draft-only upload (no review submission)

If you want to stage a build without triggering review:
```bash
task cws:upload
```
Then manually click **Submit for review** in the dev-console when
ready.

### Staged rollout to trusted testers

Publish to a limited group first:
```bash
task cws:publish:trusted
```
Requires setting up the "Trusted Testers" group in the dashboard first
(under **Distribution**).

---

## File locations at a glance

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Taskfile | `Taskfile.yml` |
| Env template | `.env.example` (in git) |
| Actual credentials | `.env` (gitignored) |
| Built extension | `apps/chrome-ext/dist/` |
| Packaged zip | `filemark.zip` (gitignored) |
| Manifest (source) | `apps/chrome-ext/public/manifest.json` |
| This runbook | `private-repo/markdown-viewer-chrome-ext/PUBLISHING.md` |
